CRANES PART1 NATIONAL FOREWORD

VOCABULARY
GENERAL

This Indian Standard which is identical with IS0 4306-l : 1990 `Cranes - Vocabulary Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ) was Part 1 : General', issued by the International adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on the recommendations of the Cranes, Lifting Chains and its Related Equipment Sectional Committee ( HMO 14 ) and approval of the Heavy Mechanical Engineering Division Council. This standard is being published Part 2 Part 3 Part 4 Part 5 Mobile cranes Tower cranes J'ib cranes Overhead travelling cranes and portal bridge cranes Standard' appear referring to this standard, they in five parts. Other parts of this standard are as follows:

Wherever the words `International should be read as `Indian Standard'. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

IS0 4306-l is a trilingual edition in English, French and Russian. As the Indian Standard is the national implementation of IS0 4305-1, only the English language text has been retained while adopting it in this standard. For French and Russian texts, reference should be made to the original IS0 publication. The standard on glossary of terms for cranes ( IS 5532 ) was first puhlished in 1969. Consequent on the availability of IS0 4306 ( in four parts ), IS 5532 was revised to adopt IS0 4306 an.d was published in tour parts under dual number system. IS0 4306 has subsequently been revised. Part 1 of IS0 4306 now covers all parts of IS 5532. Accordingly, IS 5532 is being withdrawn and IS0 4306 ( in five parts ) is being published again under dual number system.

IS04306 establishes a vocabulary in

English, French and Russian of the most commonly used terms in the field of cranes. This part of IS0 4306 defines terms concerning the main types of crane, parameters, component

1

Types of crane

1.1

Classification of cranes by construction

1.1.1

overhead type crane: Crane with its load-handling device hung from a crab or a hoist or a jib crane capable of travelling along a bridge.

1.1.1.1

overhead travelling crane: Crane with its bridge girders directly supported on rail tracks by travelling carriages.

1.1.1.2

portal bridge crane: Crane with the bridge girders supported on the rail tracks by legs.

1.1.1.3

semi-portal bridge crane: Crane with its bridge girders supported on the rail track directly at one end and by legs at the other end.

IS 13473 ( Part 1 ) : 1992 IS0 4306-l : 1990

1.1.2

cable type crane : Crane with a load-handling
a trolley travelling

device suspended

from

along track ropes secured to masts.

1.1.2.1

cable

crane:

Crane whose

supporting

elements

are ropes secured

to the tops of supporting

masts.

1.1.2.2

portal

cable crane:

Crane whose

supporting

elements

are ropes

secured at the ends of a portal bridge mounted

on two legs.

1.1.3

jib type crane : Crane with a load-handling device suspended from a jib or from a crab travelling along the jib.

either

1.1.3.1

portal dewing crane: Travelling slewing crane mounted on a portal capable of allowing railcars or road vehicles to pass under it.

1.1.3.2 semi-portal stewing crane: Travelling slewing crane mounted on a semi-portal capable of allowing railcars or road vehicles to pass under it.

_
1.1.3.3 mobile crane: Jib crane, which may be fitted with a mast (tower attachment), capable of travelling, laden or unladen, without the need for fixed runways and which relies on gravity for stability.

1.1.3.4

tower crane: Slewing jib type crane with jib located at the top of a vertical tower.

1.1.3.5

railway crane : Crane installed on a special platform travelling on railway tracks.

1.1.3.6 floating crane: Crane mounted on a special self-propelled or towed pontoon designed for its support and transport.

1.1.3.8

derrick crane (mast crane) : Slewing crane with a jib hinged at the lower part of a vertical mast which is supported at the top and the bottom.

1.1.3.8.1 guy-derrick crane: Derrick crane with the top of the mast held by means of guy ropes.

_-

1.1.3.8.2

rigid-braced derrick crane : Derrick mast held by means of rigid bracing.

cantilever crane: Jib crane with a load-handling device suspended either from a rigidly secured cantilever (a jib) or from a crab travelling along the cantilever.

1.1.3.9.1

Cantilever crane either capable of rotating on a pillar fixed at its base to a foundation, or secured to a pillar which can rotate in a support socket in its foundation.

Classification

of cranes

by the mode

of movement

1.3.1

fixed base crane: stationary base.

Crane fixed on a foundation or on any other

1.3.2

climbing crane: Crane mounted on elements of a building being built and travelling upwards by its own mechanisms as the height of the building increases.

1.3.3

portable crane: Crane mounted on a base capable of being moved from site to site manually or by means of auxilian/ equipment.

1.3.4

radial crane: Crane capable of moving around a stationary vertical axis in operation.

~~.-.-__._._. 1.3.5.1 self-propelled crane: Travelling crane equipped with a mechanism for travelling while in operation and for moving from site to site.

1.3.5.2

trailer crane: Travelling crane not provided with power for travelling which can be towed as a trailer by a tractor.

2.2.4

hook approach, C : Minimum horizontal distance between the centre cf the track rail and the vertical axis of the load-handling device.

2.2.5

tail radius. r : Maximum radius of the stewing part of the crane that lies opposite to the boom.

2.2.6

load-lifting height, H : Vertical distance from the level of the plane on which the crane is resting up to the load-handling device when it is located at its uppermost working position :

- for hooks and forks, up to their bearing surface;
- for other load-handling attachments, up to their lowest point (when closed). For overhead tvpe cranes, the lifting height is to be measured from the ground level. The lifting height is to be determined without load, the crane being erected on a level site.

17

IS 13473(Part1):1992 IS0 4306-l : 1990

2.2.7

load-lowering height, h : Vertical distance between the crane bearing level and the load-handling device located at its lowest working position :

- for hooks and forks, up to their bearing surface;
- for other load-handling attachments, up to their lowest point (when closed). For overhead type cranes, the load-lowering height is to be measured up to the rail level. The load lowering height is to be determined without any load, the crane being erected on a level site.

2.2.8

lifting range, D : Vertical distance between the highest and the lowest working positions of the load-handling device [D = H + h (see 2.2.6 and 2.2.7)1.

2.2.9

crane track height, H, : Vertical distance between the ground (floor) level and the rail head level of the crane track.

.General concepts

Motions

lifting (lowering) of load: Displacement of a load in a vertical direction.

3.1.2

3.1.3

derricking (luffing) : Angular

of the jib in a vertical plane.

3.2

Crane

stability

3.2.1

crane stability:

Ability of crane to resist tipping moments.

_

-.___
conditions : Ability of crane to resist tipof the load Q, inertia forces I, induced by the weight

3.2.3

stability under no-load condition (crane assembled): Ability of crane to resist tipping moments induced by wind load and other causes when the crane is not in operation.

I
3.3 Tests

3.3.1

static tests: Testing of a crane by applying a static load at the loadhandling device, exceeding by X % the load-lifting capacity of the crane.

3.3.2

dynamic tests: Testing of a crane by executing operating motions under a load exceeding by Y % the load-lifting capacity of the crane.

5

Limiting and indicating

devices

5.1

Rated capacity and motion limiting and indicating devices

5.1.1

limiting device (limiter) : Device which initiates stopping or restricting crane motion or function. The majority of these devices will operate automatically when the respective motion or function reaches its limiting position.

5.1.2

function limiter: Limiting device which initiates the stopping and/or restriction of designated crane function(s).

6.1.3

net loed: Load, having mass mNL, which is lifted by the crane and suspended from the fixed load-lifting attachment(s). Mass mNL is the sum of the payload mpL and the non-fixed load-lifting attachment(s)

61.4

fixed load-lifting attachment: Any equipment, having mass mFA, from which the net load may be suspended and which is permanently fastened to the lower end(s) of the hoist medium(s). Fixed load-lifting attachments are part of the crane.

6.1.5

hoist medium load: Load, having mass mHL, which is lifted by the crane and suspended from the lower end(s) of the hoist medium. Mass mHL is the sum of the payload mpL, the non-fixed load-lifting attachment(s) mNA and the fixed load-lifting attachment mFA :
mHL = mPL + mNA + II)FA
